html:
SMTO-CFG-0099 — This request doesn't fit Plan mode

GUID: a8986de9-5a80-5e6e-b98d-55bf7e857f4e
Slug: plan-protocol
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: collaboration

What happened

  • In Plan mode the Agent only looks around and asks questions, then writes one plan for you to approve. Something broke that rule, such as trying to make a change, so SMTO blocked it. Blocked changes didn't run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. For a planning request, choose Plan in the Agent mode menu in the message box, not Ask. Plan needs to look at your files and systems, which Ask mode can't do.
  2. When you want changes made, wait for the plan, then select Yes, implement this plan on the plan card, or switch Agent mode to Agent. Plan mode blocks every change on purpose until you approve a plan.
  3. If the Agent couldn't finish a plan, send a shorter, more specific request, for example naming the goal and the files or systems involved. SMTO stops after three badly formed plan attempts; a clearer request helps the Agent write one complete plan.

What success looks like

  • A plan card titled Implement this plan? appears under the Agent's answer.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't resend the identical request; change the request or the Agent mode first, or it will be blocked the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Plan-mode rules rejected the turn: unsupported collaboration_mode or Plan combined with advisory agent_mode, invalid clarification choices, a non-read or detached operation under Plan, or a malformed, empty, oversized (over 64,000 characters) or duplicate proposed_plan block.

What this means

  • Plan protocol rejects unsupported mode/advisory combinations, invalid clarification choices, disallowed mutation/unsafe/detached actions or malformed/empty/oversized/duplicate proposed-plan output. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • Plan protocol rejects unsupported mode/advisory combinations, invalid clarification choices, disallowed mutation/unsafe/detached actions or malformed/empty/oversized/duplicate proposed-plan output.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the specific Plan reason to distinguish action restrictions from plan-output formatting; do not assume every rejection is a parser error.

How to fix it

  • Check the run events (plan.mutation_blocked, plan.rejected) and the task status for the specific reason. Use Plan with Agent or Conversation mode (not advisory), keep Plan tool calls read-only and captured, give clarification questions 2–4 unique options with a valid recommended_id, and finalize with exactly one proposed_plan tagged block; use the plan implementation action when execution is intended.
  • Correct the specific Plan-mode or output-format violation; use the explicit implementation flow when execution is intended.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected supported mode admits only its allowed actions and produces one valid bounded plan artifact.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
